MESA CORE v0.8.1 · INSIDE THE ENGINE

How information moves through MESA.

Two paths: turning a source into stored memory, and finding evidence when an application asks a question. Each section below has a UML diagram, the reason behind the design and a link to its decision record.

ComponentsWrite pathStatesRead pathData modelDeployment

THE WHOLE SYSTEM AT A GLANCE

One application outside. One storage owner inside.

In the supported V4 topology, one combined process owns the API, the background workers and all three stores. The boxes are modules inside that process, not separate servers.

WHY

SQLite, LanceDB and Kùzu cannot share one transaction, and two writers on the same files make recovery ambiguous. So one process writes, SQLite records every step, and the other stores follow it.

ADR 0009 · Ledger and single owner →

01 · THE WRITE PATH

From exact source text to usable memory.

Your application sends exact text with its document, revision and chunk identity. The API accepts the work right away and returns 202; the rest happens in the background. Your application asks for the status until it reaches a final state.

Developer detail · the six steps with their code names
  1. 01

    Check the session and source

    The server derives access scope from the authenticated session. The request identifies a dataset, document, revision and exact source chunk.

    POST /v4/memory/insert
  2. 02

    Accept the work durably

    A candidate, mutation ledger record and pipeline run are created. HTTP 202 confirms admission; it does not confirm completed processing.

    MemoryCandidate · memory_mutations · pipeline_runs
  3. 03

    Extract structured facts

    A model extracts zero or more subject–relation–object facts, keeping the link to the supporting text.

    FactExtractionService → 0..N FactCandidate
  4. 04

    Apply the selected validation

    Mode 0 uses deterministic checks; mode 1 adds one model validator; mode 2 requires two distinct provider/model pairs to agree.

    MESA_TIER3_MODE = 0 / 1 / 2
  5. 05

    Write the stores in order

    Canonical facts go to SQLite, then vectors to LanceDB, then relationships to Kùzu. Each stage waits for its predecessor.

    SQL_APPLIED → VECTOR_APPLIED → GRAPH_APPLIED
  6. 06

    Confirm completion

    The client checks the durable mutation status. COMMITTED is the successful final state.

    GET /v4/mutations/{id}

WHAT IF A STEP FAILS?

Every mutation ends in a state you can see.

The three stores do not share a single database transaction. Durable work records, expiring ownership leases and idempotent receipts let the system retry or reconcile unfinished work without calling it a success.

WHY

A failed projection should be visible as retry, DLQ or BLOCKED instead of being hidden behind a compensating write.

ADR 0009 · Ledger and single owner →

02 · THE READ PATH

From a question to source-linked evidence.

The session fixes which datasets may be read. Eligibility rules remove everything else before any ranking. Four lanes then search the same eligible set in parallel, and their rankings are merged.

Search returns evidence

Hits keep assertion, document, revision, chunk and lane identity. A graph path keeps its supporting assertions and directions.

Context fits the model’s input

The context endpoint packs evidence once into a token budget. A complete graph proof fits together or not at all; your application’s model then writes the answer.

WHY

Vector, keyword and graph scores live on different scales, so adding them is meaningless. Fusing rank positions avoids that; low graph centrality is never treated as evidence that a fact is false.

ADR 0010 · RRF and PageRank →
Optional adaptive search: when is the question reformulated?

Search and context default to a single query. When adaptive context is explicitly requested, an empty result or insufficient multi-lane support can trigger one planner call and up to two reformulations. Every search keeps the original scope; this does not generate an answer.

ADR 0015 · Adaptive query planning →
Ranking formula and search limits

WHO MAY READ WHAT?

Scope comes from the server. Every fact points to its source.

Tenants own workspaces, workspaces own datasets, datasets own documents. A document has immutable revisions made of exact source chunks, and every assertion points back to the chunks that support it.

WHY

An agent ID describes a persona, not an owner. Treating a client-supplied ID as the boundary made ownership ambiguous, so the server resolves the whole chain itself.

ADR 0011 · Tenant/dataset authorization →

WHERE DOES IT RUN?

One process, one folder of data.

All three stores are embedded: they are files under one storage root, opened by one Python process. There is no separate database server to run.

Configured bounds

Limits from the v0.8.1 source, not measured latency or capacity. No benchmark has been published yet.

Context budget
2048 tokens by default
Graph search
≤ 20 seeds · ≤ 3 hops · ≤ 500 hits
Graph request timeout
15 s by default
Rank fusion
RRF, k = 60, lane weight 1.0
SDK status polling
every 2 s by default
Storage writers
exactly one process per storage root

03 · HOW THE CODE IS ASSEMBLED

Separate modules, explicit responsibilities.

mesa_api / mesa_mcp

Entry points

Receive HTTP or MCP requests and bind them to an authenticated session.

mesa_workers

Background work

Consume durable ingestion, projection and maintenance work.

mesa_memory

Information processing

Own extraction, validation, embeddings and context building.

mesa_storage

Records and search

Own canonical SQLite state, source ownership, projections and retrieval through MemoryDAO.

mesa_client

Application connection

Provides synchronous and asynchronous Python clients for the HTTP boundary.

WHY

Imports may only point down the layers. A CI check rejects reverse imports, so storage code can never depend on the API.

ADR 0013 · Production dependencies →
